payload.author: wjames111
payload.body:
## 🤖 Multi-Agent Code Review — PR #1881 (MUI v5 → v7)

**Verdict: 🔴 BLOCKERS FOUND — 1 high-priority blocker (2 call sites)**

6 specialized agents reviewed this PR (Security, Architecture, Testing, UX, Standards, Financial-Reporting). Overall this is a **clean, disciplined migration** — the UX agent script-validated 100% of Grid v2 (`item xs=` → `size={{…}}`) and `ListItem`→`ListItemButton` conversions with zero dropped breakpoints or arithmetic mismatches, tests were adapted to real v7 behavior (not weakened, net +5 assertions), and financial calculations are byte-for-byte intact. One real regression must be fixed before merge.

### 🔴 Blocker — `theme.alpha(...)` runtime crash (severity 9.5)
The codemod replaced the standalone `alpha()` import with `theme.alpha(...)`. `alpha` is a standalone export of `@mui/material` / `@mui/system` in **both** v5 and v7 — it is **not** a method on the theme object, and `src/theme.ts` does not attach one (0 `alpha` refs). This throws `TypeError: theme.alpha is not a function` at render. Only 2 call sites exist in the codebase; both are new in this diff and both are broken. See inline comments on `ApprovalProcess.tsx:29` and `TotalSalaryRequested.tsx:38`. Fix: restore `import { alpha } from '@mui/material'` and call `alpha(...)`.

### 🟡 Medium (non-blocking)
- **`Hidden` → `useMediaQuery` SSR/hydration flash** (`CoachingDetail.tsx`, `MonthlyGoal.tsx`) — all breakpoint mappings verified faithful; the only residual is a one-frame flash inherent to v7 removing `Hidden`. Accepted tradeoff.
- **CoachingDetail sidebar unmounts on drawer close** — see inline comment on `CoachingDetail.tsx:167`. Confirm no mount-time side effects are lost.
- **`AnnouncementAction.test.tsx`** — two `text`-variant tests now assert `toHaveClass('MuiButton-text')` instead of computed background (jsdom can't resolve v7's `var(--variant-textBg)`); color assertions preserved. Defensible, not a regression mask.

### 🔵 Suggestions
- **`FilterList.tsx:77`** — `primaryTypographyProps` is deprecated in v7 (use `slotProps={{ primary: {…} }}`). Renders, logs a console deprecation. See inline comment.
- **`NavBar.tsx`** — restructures the mobile account-list drawer (more than a codemod for a "chore" PR); correct and localized, just flagging scope.
- **`PartnerCare.tsx`** — a display-only `ListItem` dropped its `button` prop without becoming `ListItemButton` (no `onClick`, so only ripple styling lost).

### ✅ Cleared by review
- **Security:** supply chain coherent (all `@mui/*` from npm registry, 7.3.x line); removed `@mui/base` patch was a UX fix, correctly dropped — no residual vulnerable pin. No injection/env/auth/secret surface touched.
- **Financial:** `Hidden`→`useMediaQuery` mappings and all `currencyFormat`/arithmetic byte-for-byte intact; `convertedAmount` still used.
- **Standards:** no `export default`, `any`, `@ts-ignore`, non-null assertions, debug output, or `new Date()` introduced.
- **Fix-one-fix-all:** the `theme.alpha` issue is fully scoped — exactly 2 sites, no other color utilities mis-rewritten.

---
_Reply `/dismiss: <reason>` on a comment to dismiss a finding with severity < 7. The blocker (severity 9.5) cannot be dismissed._

## 🤖 Multi-Agent Code Review — PR #1873

### Headline
**The "Presenting Your Goal" total re-sums a subset of fields client-side and omits the always-applied ×1.06 attrition factor, so the donor-facing "Total Support Goal" systematically understates the admin's authoritative `monthlyGoal`.** See the inline comment on `PresentingYourGoalStep.tsx`. The established sibling `GoalCalculator` deliberately folds attrition in (`…/PresentingYourGoal.tsx:41  ministryExpenses: ministryExpensesTotal + attrition`); this new step drops it and doesn't even query `attrition`. Tests miss it because the mock is rigged so the 6 fields sum to exactly `monthlyGoal` (15860).

### Verified clean / refuted (no action)
- **Null `calculations`** — schema is `NewStaffGoalCalculationCalculations!` with all `Float!` subfields; dropping the old `?? 0` guard is correct. Parent is nullable but guarded in both consumers.
- **Coaching vs hrTools layout** — coaching page renders `GoalSettingsForm` directly (intended split); hrTools wraps `NsGoalCalculator` in exactly one `NsGoalCalculatorLayout` (no double/lost wrap).
- **Apollo cache / codegen / mutation refresh** — `id` present, embedded value-object needs none, all 9 fields exist in `schema.graphql`, mutation re-selects the fragment. Clean.

Substance is display-only (no auth, no mutations, non-null types), so effective operational risk ≈ MEDIUM, elevated to **HIGH** by the confirmed financial finding. Fake `$3,624` special-needs placeholder shown as real money · 403(b) values missing per-person `aria-label` · unused `goalCalculation` prop on `ReviewYourCalculationStep` (4-agent consensus) · loading/error states render flush to edge · inline error Alert + global snackbar double-surface (informational, not a violation).

Engine pre-flight selected the panel; 4 substantive specialists (security, architecture, testing, standards) ran on the engine/config/command code. 22 findings (severities modest, mostly 4–6). _Advisory — and a deliberate self-test._

---

# PR #1858 Dogfood Review: Agent-Review Engine (Reviewer Reviewing Itself)

## Executive summary

The agent-review engine is a well-built, unusually well-tested piece of multi-repo review tooling: cleanly layered pure-core modules, 58 passing node:test cases, consistent CommonJS, escaped regexes, and shell-free `execFileSync` subprocess calls (no command injection, no ReDoS, no secret leakage found). The substantive issues are not in the pure scoring core but at the seams: two parallel entry points and three arg parsers drift, the refactored command gates engine features by grepping raw YAML instead of the parsed config, and `yarn review run` hardcodes a scope that inflates its preflight risk relative to the real review path. Most security findings are lower-severity hardening items; the one structural trust-boundary concern is the auto-fix design (LLM-emitted shell run via `apply_all.sh`).

## BLOCKING

**1. Review command runs model-emitted bash (sed auto-fixes) via `apply_all.sh`** (sev 5, security)
`.claude/commands/agent-review.md:403-412, 1284-1297` — Agents write `sed -i` scripts derived from attacker-influenceable diff/file content to `/tmp/automated_fixes/*.sh`, then `apply_all.sh` auto-loops `bash "$fix"` over them. Untrusted diff -> generated shell -> executed shell. **Fix:** gate each fix behind explicit human confirmation, constrain edits to the changed-file set, prefer `git apply` of structured patches over free-form sed, never auto-run; document the scripts as untrusted.

**2. Agent over-selection from trigger keywords inside the reviewer's own rule docs** (sev 6, dogfood — see meta section)
`data-integrity`, `ux`, `financial` agents auto-selected because `content:mutation` / `content:<Formik` / `content:amount` triggers appear in `.claude/review/rules/*.md` prose, not code. **Fix:** exclude `.claude/review/rules/**` and doc markdown from content-trigger scanning, or scan only added code lines.

**3. `yarn review run` hardcodes `scope=multi_feature`, diverging from the real risk score** (sev 6, architecture)
`.claude/review/cli.cjs:108` — `buildPlan` is called with `scope:'multi_feature'` (1.3x multiplier) while `agent-review.md` Stage 0 and `plan.cjs:35` default to `single_feature` (1.0x). The same diff can land in a different LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL band depending on entry point, contradicting "engine is the single source of truth" (agent-review.md:172). **Fix:** default `run` to `single_feature`, or accept `--scope` and thread it through; centralize the default in one constant.

**4. Two parallel CLI dispatchers with duplicated logic and divergent yarn wiring** (sev 5, architecture)
`.claude/review/cli.cjs:24-37, 69-95` — Flows exist both in `cli.cjs` and in `require.main` blocks of `learningsStore.cjs`/`indexStore.cjs`/`impact.cjs`/`plan.cjs`; `package.json` wires some scripts to `cli.cjs` and others to the per-module CLIs (two arg conventions). emit/filter learning steps are reachable only via the module CLI, never the `run` orchestrator. **Fix:** make `cli.cjs` the only dispatcher, reduce module `require.main` blocks to thin shims, point all yarn scripts at `cli.cjs`, and extract one shared `changedFiles`/`parseArgs`.

**5. Command gates engine features by grepping raw `config.yml` instead of parsed config** (sev 5, architecture)
`.claude/commands/agent-review.md:292, 1194` — `grep -q "enabled: true"` is unscoped (matches both `index:` and `learning:` blocks), and `grep -q "learning:"` matches key presence not `learning.enabled`. The engine already exposes parsed `cfg.index.enabled`/`cfg.learning.enabled` (cli.cjs:110). A formatting change silently breaks gating. **Fix:** surface gate decisions f

## 🔍 Multi-Agent Code Review — Verdict: ✅ APPROVED WITH SUGGESTIONS

5 specialized agents (Architecture, Testing, Standards, UX, Financial Reporting) + dependency analysis. Standard mode.

**0 blockers.** 1 Important finding (severity 7.0–7.9) strongly recommended before merge — it cannot be dismissed via `/dismiss`. The rest are Medium/Suggestion.

### Risk: 8/10 (HIGH)
7 touched feature components + money-display logic. No auth/GraphQL/schema/dependency changes.

### Top finding (5-agent consensus)
**`AccountInfoBox.tsx:49` — `{overallBalance && (...)}` renders a stray `0` when the total is exactly `$0.00`.** `{0 && <X/>}` evaluates to `0`, which React renders as a text node — not `$0.00`, not nothing. Plausible now that fully-spent Return Travel / Re-Entry funds can offset others. Guard on `overallBalance !== undefined` and add a `overallBalance={0}` test.

---

### Findings on related lines (not in a diff hunk — can't be line-anchored)

**[Medium · 6.0/10] `BalanceCardList.tsx:64-65` — `transfersIn`/`transfersOut` type lies, risking `$NaN`.** `BalanceCardProps` declares these as required `number`, but the list passes `transferTotals[fund.fundType]?.in` (`number | undefined`). `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is off, so TS stays silent; at runtime a fund absent from `transferTotals` → `currencyFormat(undefined)` → `$NaN` on the selected card. The two new fund types raise the odds of a fund with zero transactions. Fix: `transferTotals[fund.fundType]?.in ?? 0` (and `.out`). This is the same falsy/undefined-money anti-pattern as the top finding — fix both consistently.

### Dependency note (non-blocking)
`AccountInfoBox` has 4 consumers (TransfersPage, PartnerRemindersReport, MPGAIncomeExpensesReport, StaffExpenseReport). The new `overallBalance` prop is optional → backward-compatible. **Behavior change:** the account-id `<Typography>` + tooltip now render only when `accountId` is truthy (previously always rendered). The 3 legacy consumers pass a possibly-`undefined` `accountId` during load — runtime-safe and a UI improvement, but any test asserting the `account-id` testid in a no-id/loading state may need updating.

### ✅ Verified clean
Named exports · i18n (`Trans`/`t()`) · Luxon (no `new Date()`) · no `any`/`@ts-ignore`/console/debugger · `styled` + `shouldForwardProp` typing · theme tokens all exist (`chipYellowDark`, `chartGray`, `chartBlue`) · display-boundary rounding · `funds` unpaginated (no client-sum truncation) · parentheses give a non-color negative indicator.

### To verify with product/API
- Confirm `Fund.endBalance` is guaranteed single-currency (no `currencyCode` field exists in the schema; this PR is the first to aggregate across funds while hardcoding `'USD'`).
- Confirm the account ID == the "Person Number" the tooltip describes.

| Testing | 1 | 4 | High |

# MPD Supervisor Report (PR #1855) — Consolidated Review

## Executive Summary

PR #1855 adds a new MPD Supervisor Report page that is **entirely mock-data-driven** — there are no live GraphQL queries, mutations, or backend aggregation yet (acknowledged via `TODO(MPDX)` comments). Overall risk is **low for the current diff**: the architecture is idiomatic, money is formatted only at the display boundary, the shared `MultiPageHeader` change is purely additive (zero blast radius across 29 dependents), and the code is largely a11y-conscious. The headline concerns are **forward-looking data-modeling decisions that will ossify into real bugs once the backend lands** (hardcoded currency, quarter columns derived from a single row, missing-data rendered as `$0.00`) plus a runtime-reactive **localization bug in the quick-filter labels** that is live today.

## BLOCKING (8-10)

None.

## IMPORTANT (5-7)

### 1. Quick-filter labels frozen at import-time language; never react to language change — sev 6
**`Filters/mpdSupervisorReportFilters.ts:498-515`** (ux)
`quickFilters` is a module-level constant whose `label` values come from `i18n.t('All people')` etc., evaluated once at import. Unlike every other string in the PR (which uses the `t` from `useTranslation()` and re-renders), these chip labels stay in the import-time/fallback language when the user switches languages. This is a **live bug**, not forward-looking.
**Fix:** Store only enum ids in the constant; translate at render time inside `MpdSupervisorReportFilterPanel` (e.g. a `quickFilterLabel(t, id)` helper or id→`t('...')` record). Keep literals as `t('...')` so `yarn extract` still captures them.

### 2. Team/Employment-type option text untranslated and conflated with enum values — sev 5
**`Filters/MpdSupervisorReportFilterPanel.tsx:451-472`** (ux)
Team options render raw mockData strings (`'Campus'`, `'FamilyLife'`) with no `t()`, and `MpdSupervisorReportEmploymentTypeEnum.FullTime = 'Full time'` doubles the stored filter value as the English display label (compared against `user.userPersonType`). This bakes display text into data/enum values rather than mapping codes to labels — it will propagate untranslated labels and value/label coupling when wired to the backend.
**Fix:** Define employment types as opaque codes (e.g. `'full_time'`) separate from a `t('Full time')` label; map team/option codes to translated labels at render. At minimum, comment that team names are intentionally untranslated proper nouns.

### 3. `any` types in `jest.mock` factories violate no-any-in-test-types rule — sev 5
**`MpdSupervisorReport.test.tsx:555-601`** (testing)
The `InfiniteList`/`useMockInfiniteStaff` mocks type `jest.requireActual` and props/item as `any` with eslint-disable. `testing.md` forbids `any` in test types; an `any`-typed mock cannot catch prop/return-shape drift from the real module — the exact regression these mocks should guard.
**Fix:** Type the react require with `typeof import(...)`, type `InfiniteList` props with the real generic over `EmployeeData`, and type `item` as `EmployeeData`.

## MINOR (1-4)

**Currency / financial correctness**
- **`StaffMemberRow/StaffMember.tsx` (FiscalYearQuartersBase) — sev 4** (financial): Payroll currency hardcoded to `'USD'`; `QuarterStatus` has no `currencyCode`. Harmless on mock, but will mislabel non-USD payroll once wired. Add `currencyCode` to the model now and pass `quarter.currencyCode` into `currencyFormat`.
- **`StaffMemberRow/StaffMember.tsx` (FiscalYearQuartersBase) — sev 3** (financial): Missing/NaN payroll renders as a confident `$0.00` (`currencyFormat` coerces NaN→0). When backed by real data, allow `payroll?:

payload.author: zweatshirt
payload.body:
## 🤖 Multi-Agent Code Review — ✅ CLEAN

**Verdict: CLEAN** — no issues found across 5 specialized agents (Architecture, Testing, Standards, UX, Financial Reporting). Unanimous, high confidence.

### What this PR does
Removes the MUI `required` prop (the asterisk + `aria-required`) from the `mhaAmount` and `spouseMhaAmount` `AutosaveTextField` inputs in `MhaRequestSection.tsx`.

### Why it's correct
- `required` is a passthrough to MUI `TextField` — purely visual. Validation is driven by the separate `schema` prop.
- The Yup schema in `useMhaRequestData.ts` builds these fields via `amount(...)` **without** `{ required: true }`, and `yupHelpers.ts` only attaches `.required()` when that flag is set. So these fields were never validated as required — the asterisk was misleading. Removing it aligns the UI with the actual (optional) validation and removes a false `aria-required` (an a11y improvement).
- **Convention confirmed:** every sibling SalaryCalculator field pairs the visual `required` prop with `required: true` in its schema (`MaxAllowableSection`, `RequestedSalaryCard`, `ApprovalProcessCard`, `EffectiveDateStep`). `MhaRequestSection` was the lone outlier; this diff brings it in line.
- **Financially inert:** empty amounts safely coalesce to `0` via `?? 0` across all consumers; `progressPercentage` divisor is guarded. No NaN / divide-by-zero risk.
- **No stale tests:** no test asserts the asterisk or `aria-required` on these fields, so no test update was required.

### Risk
Score 1/10 (LOW). Reviewer level: ANY. Single consumer (`YourInformation.tsx`); no breaking changes.

payload.author: zweatshirt

## 🤖 Multi-Agent Code Review — Verdict: ✅ CLEAN

**Risk: 6/10 (MEDIUM)** · standard mode · agents across the review: Architecture, Testing, Standards, Data Integrity, UX, Financial + dependency analysis

No blockers, no Important findings — only two sub-5 suggestions (inline). The feature is sound and independently verified.

### What this PR does
Adds an opt-in `deferErrorsUntilTouched` flag to the shared `useAutoSave` hook (default `false`), enabled in the questionnaire wrapper so validation errors stay hidden until a field is touched — avoiding a wall of errors on arrival. Every questionnaire field is also marked `required` (asterisk + `aria-required`) so mandatory-ness stays visible even while errors are deferred.

### Verified safe
- **Validity gating preserved (Data Integrity, High confidence):** error *display* is deferred, but `markValid`/`markInvalid` is unchanged and independent of `touched` — a user **cannot** Continue past hidden-but-invalid fields. Only the visual error is gated.
- **Backward compatible (dependency analysis):** `useAutoSave` has 5 consumers; only the questionnaire wrapper opts in. With the flag defaulting `false`, the 4 other forms (PdsGoalCalculator, SalaryCalculator, GoalCalculator ×2) are byte-identical in behavior. `showError` reduces exactly to the original condition when the flag is off.
- **Accessibility (UX, High confidence):** `aria-required` is valid on `role=radiogroup` and necessary (MUI's `FormControl required` does not propagate it to the group). The `required` work resolves the earlier concern that deferring errors left untouched required fields with no programmatic signal.
- **Standards:** clean pass — named exports, localization, no `any`, no unused imports, MUI `sx` conventions.

### Suggestions (severity < 5 — informational, non-blocking)
See inline comments. In brief: (1) the two `MinistryDetails` selects have `required` but no explicit test assertion; (2) minor display caveats of the touched-state flag. Neither blocks merge.

## 🤖 Multi-Agent Code Review — PR #1842

**Verdict: 🔴 BLOCKERS FOUND** · Risk **6/10 (MEDIUM)** · 6 specialized agents + dependency analysis (standard mode)

Two blockers must be resolved before merge:

1. **The headline feature doesn't work in production.** `useFilteredFunds` compares `selectedCategories` (raw enums like `MINISTRY_REIMBURSEMENT`) against `category.category`, which `MPGAIncomeExpensesReport.tsx:98` has already localized to a display label (`Ministry Reimbursement`). `.includes(category.category.toUpperCase())` → `"MINISTRY_REIMBURSEMENT"` vs `"MINISTRY REIMBURSEMENT"` (underscore vs space) → never matches for multi-word categories. Single-word categories (`Donation`, `Salary`) coincidentally match, so the filter is *inconsistently* broken. CI is green because the unit test feeds raw enums and bypasses the `getLocalizedCategory` transform that production always applies. (Verified end-to-end by Data Integrity + Financial agents and by the reviewer directly.)
2. **i18n regression.** The non-MPGA branch of the new help-text ternary lost its `t()` wrapper and now renders raw English on the existing StaffExpenseReport.

See inline comments for these plus the Important (untested filter wiring) and Medium findings.

### Dependency Impact — no breaking changes
`useFilteredFunds`'s new required 2nd arg: both call sites updated. New exports (`getFiltersWithCalculatedDates`, `StyledFilterButton`) and the optional `isMpgaReport` prop are backward-compatible. `DataFields.id` is consumed only as an opaque React/DataGrid key — the new `-income`/`-expense` suffixes actually *fix* a prior row-id collision.

### Suggestions (informational, not inlined)
- **Hook sign-splitting duplication** (`useFilteredFunds.ts:96-129`): the combine branch pre-splits by sign (`>= 0`), then `pushData` re-splits (`> 0`/`< 0`). Consider summing subcategories into one signed `monthly[]` and letting `pushData` own all sign logic.
- **Redundant `.toUpperCase()`** (`useFilteredFunds.ts:75`): no-op on enums; remove once the match is fixed.
- **Missing hook test branches**: `selectedCategories === null` (default path), unchecked-per-subcategory rows, and the zero-suppression guard are all unexercised.
- **`'Filter Settings'` → `'Report Settings'`** rename is consistent across buttons/tests; old key now orphaned (harmless).

✅ Named exports · ✅ no `new Date()` (Luxon used) · ✅ no `any` · ✅ currency mixing prevented (hardcoded USD) · ⚠️ `.toFixed()` inside aggregation (matches existing convention) · ❌ null `month.total` unguarded (see inline).

payload.author: wjames111
payload.body:
## Multi-Agent Code Review

**Mode:** Standard (4 agents — Architecture, Testing, Standards, Financial Reporting)
**Risk:** LOW (2/10) — local rename + calculation simplification
**Verdict:** APPROVED_WITH_SUGGESTIONS

### Summary

Clean, mechanical refactor. The old `workCompPercentage` (a fraction of gross pay) is fully replaced by `workCompAmount` (a fixed monthly dollar amount) across all 6 files. Math walk-throughs in the test comments are arithmetically correct; lint and TS pass; named-export and i18n standards are maintained; no critical issues.

Three agents (Architecture, Standards, Financial Reporting) independently flagged the same cross-cutting concern: the GraphQL enum `PART_TIME_WORK_COMPENSATION` and its `fee: Float!` field are unchanged on the wire, but the client-side interpretation flipped from "fraction" to "dollars." If the backend `mpd_goal_misc_constants` row for this constant is not updated before this PR ships, every part-time PDS goal will silently compute workComp as ~$0.17/month instead of ~$850/month — a ~99% under-calculation invisible to the user. Confirm deploy order (backend first) and consider a defensive sanity guard. See the inline comment on `pdsGoalConstants.ts:32`.

### Findings on Related Files (Not in This PR)

These were identified during review on files related to the changes but not directly modified. They cannot be posted as line comments.

**[Important] src/components/HrTools/PdsGoalCalculator/PdsGoalCalculatorTestWrapper.tsx:259** — The shared test wrapper still mocks `PART_TIME_WORK_COMPENSATION.fee: 0.17`. With the new semantics, that value is now interpreted as $0.17/month, not 17%. Nothing breaks today (`PdsSummaryTable.test.tsx` part-time tests don't assert on workComp values), but it's a footgun for the next contributor who writes a numeric assertion against this wrapper. Recommend bumping to a realistic dollar amount (e.g., `20.35` or `400`) in this PR.
  - Severity: 7.0/10
  - Flagged by: Testing & Quality Agent
  - Recommended Action:
    ```diff
    -                fee: 0.17,
    +                fee: 20.35,
    ```

### Suggested Additional Test (Optional)

Neither the new "uses the fixed workCompAmount for part-time" test in `OtherExpenses.test.ts` nor the part-time scenario in `usePdsSummaryData.test.ts` explicitly proves that `workComp` is now **independent** of `grossMonthlyPay`. Two agents recommended adding a test like:

```ts
it('ignores grossMonthlyPay (workComp is fixed, not a percentage)', () => {
  const result = calculateOtherExpenses(partTime(), {
    ...defaultConstants,
    grossMonthlyPay: 999999,
  });
  expect(result.workComp).toBeCloseTo(680);
});
```

This catches a future regression where someone accidentally re-introduces the `grossMonthlyPay * workCompAmount` formula.

payload.title: HS-1639514 - Fix Google Import, MailChimp, Organization, and PrayerLetters redirects

payload.author: zweatshirt
payload.body:
## 🤖 Multi-Agent Code Review — ✅ CLEAN

**4 agents** (Security, Architecture, Testing, Standards) · **standard** mode · **Risk: LOW (1/10)**

No blockers, no important issues, no standards violations. This is a correct, idiomatic, net-debt-reducing SSR-safety fix. Six low-severity suggestions (all < 2.5/10), all informational.

### What the change does
Defers the `window.location.origin` read out of render and into a `useEffect` (`useState('')` default), fixing the SSR `ReferenceError: window is not defined` crash on the integrations page (introduced when `SITE_URL` was removed). Server + first hydration render use `''` (markup matches → clean hydration), then the effect populates the real origin and React patches the button hrefs.

### Consensus theme — transient host-relative `redirect_to` (all 4 agents)
During SSR / pre-hydration, `origin` is `''`, so `redirect_to` is host-relative until the effect runs. **All agents independently concluded this is functionally safe**: the `href` getters are only navigated on user click (post-hydration), and the Organization flows build the URL at click time, so `origin` is always populated by interaction time. No open-redirect risk (no user input flows into the target). Strictly better than the crash it replaces. Optional belt-and-suspenders (fall back to `window.location.origin` at call time when `origin === ''`) was considered and **not** recommended as required.

### Notes
- **Architecture:** the `useState('')`+`useEffect` choice is the correct hydration-safe pattern; explicitly *don't* copy the `typeof window` lazy-initializer from `useLocalStorage.ts` (would cause a hydration mismatch here). `useEffect([])` deps correct. Net technical debt reduced.
- **Standards:** all applicable checklist items PASS — named export, hook naming/colocation, no `any`, `@ts-expect-error` carries an explanatory comment, exact full-URL test assertions, `window` read confined to an effect.
- **"Fix one, fix all":** verified the only other `window.location.origin` reference is in `_document.page.tsx` inside a browser-executed `<script>` string (safe). No remaining instances of this bug — fix is complete.

### Suggestions (informational, no `/dismiss` needed)
- Add `getMailChimpOauthUrl` / `getPrayerlettersOauthUrl` to this hook's test (their path segments `mailchimp` / `prayer_letters` aren't pinned here — though both are covered at the component level). An `it.each` over all four getters closes it cheaply.
- Optional: assert the no-session error path (`useRequiredSession` throws).

payload.title: MPDX-9650 - Improve validation in Savings Fund Transfer

payload.author: zweatshirt
payload.body:
## 🤖 Multi-Agent Code Review — Verdict: ✅ CLEAN

**Mode:** standard · **Risk:** 1/10 (LOW) · **Blockers:** 0

Agents run: Architecture, UX/a11y, Financial (domain). Testing + Standards were verified inline (their key concerns are addressed below). This is a small, focused change — end-date validation now requires the end date to be **strictly at least one calendar day after** the transfer date (day-granular Luxon comparison), plus a permanent descriptive helper text on the End Date field, with 4 colocated tests.

### Findings
Only two severity-3 suggestions (informational — do not block merge). See the inline comment for the first; the second is below.

### Verified — concerns from skipped agents
- **Type safety:** Dropping the `as string` cast on `errors.endDate` is correct and type-safe. Because `endDate` is `DateTime<boolean> | null`, Formik's `FormikErrors` mapped type resolves it to `string | undefined` (the `| null` defeats the `extends object` branch). The sibling `transferDate` (non-nullable) resolves to a `FormikErrors<DateTime>` object — which is exactly why line 478 still needs its cast. `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- **Tests using past dates:** `12/01/2024` also fails the recurring `start-date` rule, but each new test asserts only the end-date error's presence/absence, which is independent and correct in isolation. Suite passes. Minor smell — future dates would read cleaner — but not a defect.

### Findings on Related Files (Not on Changed Lines)

**[Suggestion] TransferModal.tsx:478** — Cast asymmetry between sibling date fields
- Severity: 3.0/10 · Flagged by: Architecture
- The End Date helper (this PR) now passes `errors.endDate` directly, while the adjacent Transfer Date helper at line 478 still uses `(errors.transferDate as string)`. The new pattern is the better one; line 478 is the outlier and is out of scope here. Consider dropping that cast if the line is touched in a future PR.

### Domain note (non-blocking, pre-existing)
The submit path sends `recurringStart`/`recurringEnd` as full `toISO()` timestamps with a local offset, while validation compares at day granularity. Not reachable as a bug here (both fields are local-midnight date-only values), but worth a one-line confirmation with the API team that the backend treats these as **calendar dates**, not raw UTC instants — to avoid a boundary day-shift. This concerns the pre-existing `toISO()` submission, not the lines this PR adds.
